summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package ships a postinstall script (`node beacon.cjs`) and an import-time trigger in index.js that both POST installer-side host identifiers — package name, `os.hostname()`, install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` — to a hardcoded bare-IP destination `http://13.140.137.222:8787/_ah/dc` over plain HTTP. index.js wraps the beacon call in try/catch and exports a `Proxy({}, { get: _noop })` so the module silently resolves as a stub for any accessed member, letting it stand in for an internal package without crashing a build. The `@webapp-shared` scope and stub shape are consistent with dependency-confusion scaffolding targeting private/internal scopes; the beacon fires both at `npm install` (via the postinstall lifecycle hook) and at `require()` time, so a successful callback is delivered even when lifecycle scripts are disabled. README comments self-labelling this as an authorized test do not change the behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
